name: Tala Hua Gosht
subtitle: mutton boiled tender then fried dry with black pepper until the masala clings

ingredients.note: the dominant note of the dish

prepNotes: Marinate the mutton with the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and salt for 1 hour at room temperature, or up to overnight in the fridge.
Crush the peppercorns coarsely in a mortar just before cooking; pre-ground pepper tastes flat and dusty here.
Use a wide pan for the frying stage — the meat needs room to sit in one layer and colour.

steps.text: Pressure cook the marinated mutton with 1 sliced onion, the whole spices and 400ml water for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes.
Let the pressure fall naturally, then check: the meat should give completely to a fork. If not, cook 5 minutes more.
steps.tip: Undercooked mutton will not tenderise once you start frying it — get it right here.

steps.text: Strain, keeping the stock. Boil the stock down separately to about 100ml of concentrated liquid.
Heat the oil in a wide kadhai and fry the remaining sliced onions for 10 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add the green chillies and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 30 seconds, then tip in the drained mutton pieces.
Fry on medium-high for 12-15 minutes, turning the pieces every couple of minutes, until they are browned on all sides and the masala has dried onto them.
steps.tip: This is the whole dish. Turn, do not stir — you want colour on the meat, not a mash.

steps.text: Pour in the reduced stock a spoon at a time, letting each addition dry off before adding the next, until the pan is dry and glossy.
Add the crushed black pepper and garam masala and toss for 2 minutes off the direct heat.
steps.tip: Pepper goes in at the end; cooked long it loses its top notes.

steps.text: Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves and serve with roti or bagara khana.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan over medium heat with 1 tbsp water so it steams loose without going soggy; it is meant to be a dry dish, so avoid adding oil.
